correctness.rationale: The 24-vertex GP(12,5) graph and unique-neighbor closure are explicit. Exhaustive tests of 24 singletons, 276 pairs, and 2024 triples find 0, 0, and 576 successful configurations; independent bit-mask GP and sequential-set Cayley checkers agree and verify a 24-vertex graph isomorphism. Complete move enumeration yields 6660 jump and 1152 slide edges, and 576 BFS roots per graph give all 165600 pairwise distances. The exact maximum penalty 7 has 396 pairs (324 with lengths 1 and 8, 72 with lengths 3 and 10). A third checker verifies all 144 explicit S4-by-S3 automorphisms, all five orbits, and the 72-pair single orbit. The bipartition additionally has a direct parity proof. Each finite algorithm uses complete enumeration, not samples or unbounded assumptions.

originality.rationale: The checked arXiv framework defines power-domination reconfiguration and proves general statements for standard families; the checked cubic graph paper gives bounds, not Nauru optimum-triple or reconfiguration metrics. Publicly available same-graph calculations analyze 504 edge-colourings, 120 perfect matchings with anti-forcing sets, and a non-matching homology complex; their state spaces and conclusions cannot directly imply the 576 optimal sensor configurations, four-regular slide graph, sharp penalty, or extremal-pair orbit. Searches by GP label, Cayley alias, exact numbers, and claim-level properties returned no covering result. Unindexed-equivalence risk remains.
residual_risks: A full historical proof of uniqueness is impossible; an unindexed calculation or a different presentation of the 576-state reconfiguration might exist.
The exact finite theorem has no automatic extension to other cubic symmetric or generalized Petersen graphs.

value.rationale: The Nauru graph is a canonical arc-transitive 24-vertex cubic benchmark. Beyond a minimum cardinality census, this gives a natural complete classification of optimum-preserving sensor movement: a connected four-regular bipartite slide graph with five automorphism orbits, one 144-state exceptional-eccentricity orbit, one orbit of 72 diametral pairs, and a sharp seven-move locality penalty. All these are natural parameters of the same optimum configuration space, not arbitrary slices; they directly distinguish global reachability from optimal local relocation cost. Value is finite and structural, with no unsupported downstream or infinite-family claim.
